nome: Security and Trust Between Site and Agent

lado_card.texto: The threat side: prompt injection, confirmation, exposure, MCP server, and bot identity. The kit runs at no cost and needs no key.

inicio.titulo: Security and trust between your site and agents
inicio.lead: Prompt injection has no fix, and the vendors say so themselves. What you can do is decide what the agent sees, what it can do without you, and how your server refuses what isn't its own. Eight lessons, each with an attack running on your machine and the control that stops it.
inicio.capa_alt: Security and trust between site and agent: dark monitor with a form and a padlock, a cable plugged in beside it.

numeros.t: attacks on the MCP server in the kit

inicio.aulas_sub: Each lesson ends with a command you run and an output that checks out. The kit is in the course's own repository.

itens: People who have already done courses 1 to 3 of the track (MCP server, WebMCP on the page, browser agents) or who already have tools exposed to agents.
Web devs or technical site owners who will let an agent act on the visitor's behalf and want to know where that goes wrong.
People who run an MCP server over HTTP and want to check audience, scope, and secret before opening it to the outside.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: Mark third-party text with untrustedContentHint and use a canary to prove that no tool leaked.
Add confirmation with target and effect to every action with consequences, and test that declining changes nothing.
Measure who sees each tool (iframe, exposedTo, fromOrigins) and turn WebMCP off with Permissions-Policy.
Run 6 attacks against an MCP server, check a Web Bot Auth signature, and close with the audit of your site.

blocos.t: Where this course fits in the WebMCP Track
itens: Course 1 teaches the MCP server and OAuth; course 2, the WebMCP API on the page; course 3, the agent that uses the site. Here is the threat side of all three.
Course 5 (expert) brings it all together in production, with observability and governance.
Lethal trifecta, injection against an agent, and loop sandbox are in the LOOP-R Engineering Track (link in lessons 1 and 8).
